newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Peres, Palestinians' Arafat meet.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Peres, Palestinians' Arafat meet.

text.p: Israeli Labour party leader Shimon Peres met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Wednesday and urged him not to give up hopes for peace.
"There is no way back, only a way ahead. Nobody can change this fact," Peres said at a dinner both men attended for visiting members of the Middle East committee of the Socialist International.
"I recommend not to give up hope," said the former Israeli prime minister, who lost a national election a year ago to right-wing Likud party leader Benjamin Netanyahu.

The meeting in the self-ruled West Bank town of Ramallah was held against the backdrop of a Middle East peace process in crisis over Netanyahu's decision to build a Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem.
Peres and Arafat, along with the late Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin, shared the 1994 Nobel Peace Prize for peace accords that granted Palestinians limited self-rule.
In a blow to Peres' prestige on Tuesday, his own Labour party rejected a proposal to discuss honouring him with the title of party president.
The title would have secured Peres' party status ahead of a changing of the guard in internal elections in June in which he is not running.
A spokeswoman for Peres said the meeting with Arafat had been scheduled in advance, in the framework of the Socialist International deliberations being held in Ramallah and Tel Aviv.
